# Electronics: printed circuit boards

You design boards the way you design parts: the engine resolves, checks and outputs them. A board is `pcb.board.create { name, width, height | outline: [[x, y]…] | sketch, corner_radius?, cutouts?, layers: 2 to 32 (even), thickness: 1.6, finish: "HASL lead-free" | "ENIG" | …, mask: "green" | "black" | …, rules?, net_classes?: [{ name, nets, track_width, clearance, via_drill, via_diameter, neck_width? }], quantity?, at?: [x, y, z] }` (mm, y up, origin at the board's lower left). It returns `{ id, model }`: `model` is the board's real 3D part (FR4 with every hole; each populated component modelled as it looks: chip ends, gull-wing leads, the USB-C shell, header pins through the board, the module's can; declared as stock with its MPN and LCSC number; the view draws the mask, copper, finish and silk on it), rewritten by the engine whenever the board changes — design enclosures around it and clash-check it like any part, but edit the board, never that program. `pcb.board.outline_to_sketch { board, link? }` turns the outline into a sketch an enclosure can follow (with `link` the board follows the sketch after); `pcb.board.update { target, sketch }` makes a board follow an existing sketch's largest loop.

Components: `pcb.component.create { board, reference: "U1", footprint, value, at: [x, y], rotation (° counter-clockwise from the top), side: "top" | "bottom", mpn, manufacturer, lcsc, description, pins: { "<pad>": "<net>" }, pin_names: { "<pad>": "EN" } }`; `pcb.component.update` moves, turns, flips or re-nets one (track ends on its pads follow at 45° and are marked `reroute`; `drag_tracks: false` leaves them); `pcb.netlist.set { board, nets: { GND: ["U1.1", "C3.2"] }, replace? }` writes the whole netlist at once. Overlapping pads of one part (USB-C's paired contacts, a switch's legs) are one piece of copper and share a net. GET `/pcb/library` lists the footprints: R/C/LED in 0402/0603/0805/1206, SOT-23, SOT-23-5, SOT-223, SOIC-8, TSSOP-20, QFN-32_5x5 (all from the IPC-7351B land equations on JEDEC/EIA outlines), USB-C_16P (HRO TYPE-C-31-M-12), ESP32-WROOM-32, SW_Tactile_6x6, LED_3mm/5mm, JST_PH_n / JST_XH_n, PinHeader_1xNN_2.54 / 2xNN, MountingHole_M2/M25/M3/M3_Pad; origin at the package centre (headers and JST at pin 1), zero rotation per IPC-7351 (pin 1 left / top left). A part the library lacks: `pcb.footprint.define { board, footprint: { name, pads: [{ number, kind: smd | tht | npth, shape: rect | round_rect | circle | oval, size: [w, h], at, rotation?, drill?: [w, h] }], body: [{ shape: box | cylinder, at, size, z: [bottom, top], material }], source } }` from its datasheet's recommended land pattern — say which drawing you used.

Schematic (DE-850): draw the circuit first and the board follows it; the netlist is then traceable to symbols and wires. `pcb.schematic.create { board?, name?, paper?: "A4" | "A3" | …, title?, company?, revision? }` (one sheet "1"; `pcb.schematic.sheet { schematic, name, parent?, at?, size?, pins? }` adds sheets, hierarchical ones as a box on their parent). Place symbols with `pcb.schematic.place { schematic, symbol, reference?, value?, footprint?, at: [x, y], rotation?: 0|90|180|270, mirror?, unit?, mpn?, manufacturer?, lcsc?, description?, dnp?, pin_map?: { "<pin>": ["<pad>"…] }, pins? }` (sheet mm, y down, pins on the 1.27 mm grid; reference defaults to the next free R8/C3/U2; value, footprint, MPN and LCSC default to the symbol's). GET `/pcb/symbols` lists them: R, C, C_Polarized, L, Fuse, Crystal, D, D_Schottky, D_Zener, LED (pin 1 cathode), Q_NPN/Q_PNP (1 B, 2 E, 3 C), Q_NMOS/Q_PMOS (1 G, 2 S, 3 D), SW_Push, USB_C_16P (each signal lands on both rows' pads), LDO_SOT23-5 (ME6211), LDO_SOT223 (AMS1117), ESP32-WROOM-32E, OpAmp, OpAmp_Dual (units A, B and supply C), Conn_01xNN, Conn_02xNN, JST_PH_n, JST_XH_n, PWR_FLAG; a part the library lacks is `symbol: "IC"` with `pins: [{ number, name, type: input|output|bidirectional|tri_state|passive|power_in|power_out|open_collector|no_connect, side?, pads? }]` (drawn as a box). Connect with `pcb.schematic.wire { schematic, from: "U1.3" | [x, y], to: "R4.EN" | [x, y] }` (routed orthogonally around symbols, never touching another pin) or `points`; `pcb.schematic.label { schematic, text, kind?: local|global|hierarchical|power, pin: "C3.2" | at }` (with `pin`, on a short stub wire); `pcb.schematic.connect { schematic, net, pins: [...] }` does that for many pins (power ports for supply names: GND, 3V3, 5V, VBUS…); `pcb.schematic.no_connect { schematic, pins }` for pins left unused on purpose; `pcb.schematic.junction`, `pcb.schematic.text`, `pcb.schematic.symbol.update` (moving drags attached wires), `pcb.schematic.item.update { target, at? | delta? | points?, text?, rotation? }`, `pcb.schematic.delete { targets }`, `pcb.schematic.annotate { schematic, reset? }` numbers R? parts. Connectivity: an end on a wire or pin connects (a T joins, plain crossings do not, a junction joins them); same-named local labels join on their sheet, global labels and power ports everywhere; nets are named by power port, global, then local label, else `Net-(R1-Pad2)`. `pcb.schematic.from_netlist { schematic, parts: [{ reference, value, footprint, mpn?, lcsc?, symbol? }], nets: { GND: ["U1.1", …] } }` draws a whole netlist readably (ICs and connectors with labelled pins, two-pin parts hanging under the part they serve, supplies as ports, unused pins flagged, PWR_FLAGs where a supply comes in); `pcb.schematic.from_board { board }` does it for an existing board. GET `/pcb/schematic/<id>` returns everything drawn, `nets`, `violations` (ERC: unconnected_pin, pin_conflict, power_not_driven, single_pin_net, duplicate_reference, not_annotated, missing_footprint, unknown_footprint, pin_map, label_unmatched (a typo?), missing_unit, dangling_wire, no_connect_*, multiple_net_names; each with `objects` and `refs`) and `sync`, the pending board update; `/pcb/schematic/<id>/schematic.pdf` prints every sheet. `pcb.schematic.update_board { schematic, dry_run?, place?: { R8: { at, rotation?, side? } } }` makes the board match: parts added (in a row below the board unless placed), fields and pad nets changed, parts no symbol has removed, mounting holes and the schematic's `board_only` refs kept, all listed in its report (`added`, `changed`, `nets`, `removed`, `board_only`, `new_nets`, `gone_nets`); show the person that report, never update silently. `pcb.schematic.back_annotate { schematic }` brings reference, footprint and value changes made on the board back. Boards without a schematic keep `pcb.netlist.set`. `./ise check` includes ERC errors. `examples/pcb-esp32/schematic-steps.json` builds the same board schematic-first with identical nets.

Schematic editing beyond placing and wiring. Buses: `pcb.schematic.bus { schematic, sheet?, points, label?: "D[0..7]" }` draws a bus (named by a bus label on it: vector `D[0..7]` = D0…D7, group `{SDA SCL}`, prefixed group `I2C{SDA SCL}` = I2C.SDA, I2C.SCL, or a bus alias set with `pcb.schematic.update { bus_aliases: { "USB": ["DP", "DM", "VBUS"] } }`, used as `USB`, `{USB}` or `P1{USB}`); a bus's members are nets on its sheet (everywhere with a global bus label), joined by name with ordinary labels; a sheet pin and the hierarchical bus label inside join member by member in order (`DATA[0..7]` outside can feed `D[0..7]` inside; the parent's names win). `pcb.schematic.bus_entry { schematic, at (on the bus), size?: [±2.54, ±2.54] }` joins a wire, which takes its member from its own net label; `pcb.schematic.bus.unfold { bus, members?, side?, length? }` breaks members out in a row (entry, wire, label each). Reusable sheets: `pcb.schematic.sheet { schematic, parent, name, instance_of: "<sheet id>" }` shows another sheet's circuit again (one circuit, edits follow everywhere) with its own references (annotate numbers each instance; `pcb.schematic.symbol.update { target, instance: "<sheet>", reference }` sets one) and its own nets; `sync_pins: true` makes a box's pins match the hierarchical labels inside (inputs left, outputs right); `page` sets the printed page number. Selections: `pcb.schematic.move { targets, delta?, rotate?: 90|180|270, mirror?: "x"|"y", about?, drag? }` moves, turns or mirrors several items together (attached wires follow), `pcb.schematic.align { targets, how: left|right|top|bottom|center_x|center_y|distribute_x|distribute_y }`, `pcb.schematic.duplicate { targets, delta?, increment?, sheet? }` copies (new references; label and note numbers step by `increment`; `sheet` pastes onto another sheet). `pcb.schematic.replace { schematic, find, replace, in?: [references, values, footprints, fields, labels, texts], match_case?, whole_word?, wildcards?, dry_run? }` is find and replace. Fields: `pcb.schematic.fields { schematic, set: [{ reference | target, field, value }], rename?: [from, to], remove? }` edits many symbols at once (Value, Footprint, MPN, Manufacturer, LCSC, Description, DNP or any custom field); `pcb.schematic.update { field_templates: [{ name, value, visible }] }` gives every new symbol those fields (visible ones are drawn). Annotation: `pcb.schematic.annotate { schematic, reset?, order?: rows|columns, numbering?: continuous|sheet|sheet1000, start?, sheet?, targets?, increment? }`. ERC settings: `pcb.schematic.erc { schematic, severities?: { code: error|warning|ignore|default }, pin_matrix?: { "output/open_collector": error|warning|ok|default }, exclude?: [{ key, comment }], include?: [key], reset? }` (each violation has a `key`; excluded ones stay listed with `excluded: true` and stop counting; the view's `setup.pin_matrix` is the effective matrix over input, output, bidirectional, tri_state, passive, unspecified, power_in, power_out, open_collector, open_emitter). More ERC codes: pin_not_driven, hier_pin_unmatched, hier_label_unmatched, bus_unnamed, bus_label_on_wire, bus_wire_conflict, bus_entry_dangling, bus_entry_unlabeled, bus_member_unknown, bus_width_mismatch, multiple_bus_names, unknown_netclass. Net classes: `pcb.schematic.netclass { schematic, name, color?, wire_width?, track_width?, clearance?, via_diameter?, via_drill?, patterns?: ["USB_*"], rename?, delete? }`; a `pcb.schematic.label { kind: "directive", text: "<class>", at }` on a wire puts its net in the class; `pcb.schematic.net_color { schematic, net, color }` colours one net; nets carry `class` and `color`, and "Update board" writes the classes (nets and track rules) to the board's net classes. Graphics (no connectivity): `pcb.schematic.shape { schematic, shape: polyline|polygon|rect|circle|arc|bezier, points, width?, color?, fill?, dash?: dash|dot|dash_dot }`, `pcb.schematic.text_box { schematic, at, size, text, text_size?, justify?, border?, fill? }`, `pcb.schematic.table { schematic, at, cells: [["Rail", "V"], ["3V3", "3.3"]], col_widths?, header? }`, `pcb.schematic.image { schematic, at, width, data: <base64 PNG/JPEG or data: URI> }`; `pcb.schematic.text` takes `justify`, `angle`, `bold`, `italic`, `color`; `pcb.schematic.item.update { target, delta?, set: { … } }` changes any of them. Text variables `${TITLE}`, `${REVISION}`, `${DATE}`, `${COMPANY}`, `${SHEETNAME}`, `${#}`, `${##}`, `${COMMENT1}` and your own (`pcb.schematic.update { text_vars: { "CHECKER": "A. Ade" } }`) expand in notes, text boxes, tables and the drawing sheet; `pcb.schematic.update { drawing_sheet: { no_title_block?, no_zones?, margin?, items: [{ kind: line|rect|text, corner: rb|lb|rt|lt, at, end?, text?, size?, bold? }] } }` edits the page layout. Outputs: GET `/pcb/schematic/<id>/netlist?format=kicad|orcad|cadstar|spice`, `/bom?group=Value,Footprint&fields=Reference,Qty,Value,MPN&dnp=1` (CSV, or `format=json`), `/sheet/<n>.svg`, `/schematic.pdf`; or `./ise sch export <schematic> netlist|bom|svg|pdf [--format …] [--group …] [--fields …] [--sheet n] --out file`, `./ise sch find <schematic> <text>`, `./ise sch erc <schematic>` (with keys), `./ise sch buses <schematic>`, `./ise sch sheets <schematic>`. The person has all of it in the schematic view: box select (drag on empty paper; right-drag pans), Shift-click to add, Ctrl+A, drag a selection, R/Shift+R turn, X/Y mirror, Ctrl+C/V paste at the cursor, Ctrl+D duplicate, Insert repeats the last item with its number stepped, Ctrl+F find and replace, B bus, Z bus entry, graphics tools, double-click a sheet box to enter it (Backspace goes up), and side tabs for Sheets (hierarchy), Fields (table, CSV), Setup (net classes, bus aliases, ERC matrix and severities, field templates, text variables, drawing sheet) and Export.

Copper: `pcb.track.create { board, layer: "top" | "bottom" | "in1" … "in30", points, width?, net? }` (net from the copper under its first point, width from the net class), `pcb.route.create { board, net?, width?, runs: [{ layer, points }…] }` (one track per run, a via where each run meets the next on another layer), `pcb.via.create { board, at, net?, drill?, diameter? }`, `pcb.zone.create { board, net: "GND", layer, outline?, clearance?, min_width?, priority?, connection?: "thermal" | "thermal_tht" | "solid" | "none", thermal_gap?: 0.5, thermal_spoke?: 0.5 }` (a pour, refilled around everything else, dead islands removed; its pads join through four-spoke thermal reliefs unless solid; a pad with fewer than two spokes is a `thermal_relief` warning), `pcb.track.update`, `pcb.zone.update`, `pcb.delete { targets }`. `pcb.autoroute { board, nets?, skip?, grid?: 0.25, rip_up?: true, via_cost?: 5 }` routes unrouted nets on a grid with vias (wide nets first; a net that cannot finish rips up the autorouted nets in its way and they are routed again; then passes in a new order) and reports `routed`, `failed` with reasons, `vias` and `ripped`; it replaces its own earlier copper and dragged tracks that now break a rule. Near a net's pads it necks down to the class's `neck_width` (default 60 % of the width) and reaches off-grid pads with a short stub, so wide power leaves fine-pitch pads; its copper is ordinary tracks and vias, checked like yours. Place for routing: decoupling next to its pin, connectors at the edge.

Hand routing (the interactive router, as the person has it): `pcb.route.interactive { board, from: "R5.2" | [x, y], to: "U1.24" | [x, y] | [{ at, layer?, diagonal_first? }…], layer?, net?, mode?: "walkaround" | "shove" | "highlight", angle?: "45" | "90" | "free", width?, via_drill?, via_diameter?, optimize?: true, corners?: "sharp" | "arc", arc_radius? }` lays a route from a pad, track end or point through each step (a step on another layer starts with a via; net, width and via sizes from the net class). Walkaround goes round other nets' copper keeping every clearance (45° octagons round each obstacle, then smoothed), stopping short when there is no way (`reached: false`); shove goes round pads but pushes tracks and vias of other nets aside (pushed tracks bend round the new line on their own side, vias step out and drag their tracks; whatever moves pushes in turn), and walks round when pushing cannot work (a track end or pad in the way); highlight goes straight and reports. It returns `tracks`, `vias`, `ok`, `reached`, `mode` used, `pushed_tracks`/`pushed_vias`, `collisions` and `notes`. `pcb.route.drag { board, target, kind?: "segment" | "corner" | "arc" | "via", index, from?, to, mode?: "shove" | "highlight", angle?: "45" | "free" }` drags a track's segment sideways (neighbours keep their directions), a corner, an arc (bulged through `to`) or a via (its tracks follow at 45°), pushing what is in the way (a shove drag that would break a clearance is refused). Tracks may have arcs: `bulges` per segment (tan(sweep/4), counter-clockwise positive) on `pcb.track.create`/`update`; `pcb.track.fillet { targets, radius }` rounds corners (less where a leg is short or a clearance would break). `pcb.route.optimize { board, targets? | nets? }` smooths routed copper (runs of corners replaced by one dogleg, square corners mitred, every clearance kept, ends fixed); `pcb.route.cleanup { board, merge?, dangling?, vias? }` merges straight-through points, joins tracks that meet end to end, trims dangling stubs, removes duplicate and redundant vias (joining fewer than two layers) and reports the counts; `pcb.route.unroute { board, nets?, components?, targets? }` removes nets' copper, the copper on parts' pads, or a connection pad to pad; `pcb.track.break { target, at }` splits a track; `pcb.fanout { component, nets?, skip?, length? }` puts a short stub and a via outward from each unrouted SMD pad where it fits. From the shell: `./ise pcb route <board> <from> <to> [--mode shove] [--layer bottom]`, `./ise pcb drag <board> <track|via> <x,y> [--index 1] [--kind corner]`, `./ise pcb cleanup <board>`, `./ise pcb optimize <board>`. Preview without changing anything: `POST /pcb/<id>/router { op: "route" | "drag", … }` returns the plan. The person routes with X (click a pad or track end, click corners; a click on a pad of the net finishes; `/` flips the bend, V adds a via and changes layer, PageUp/PageDown inner layers, W/Shift+W width, Backspace undoes a corner, F finishes to the nearest pad, M cycles walkaround/shove/highlight), drags tracks and vias (Alt: free angle), U selects a connection, B breaks a track, and has Optimize, Round, Unroute, Fan out and Clean up in the board's toolbar; the clearance halo and red collision marks show while routing.

Checks: GET `/pcb/<id>` returns the board resolved (`board.pads/tracks/vias/zones/nets/ratsnest/stats`) and `board.violations`, each with `code` (clearance, short, unrouted, track_width, drill, annular_ring, edge_clearance, outside_board, courtyard_overlap, hole_to_hole, unknown_footprint; warnings single_pad_net, no_net, silk_text), `message`, `at`, `layer`, the `objects` (entity ids) and `refs` ("U1.25"). `./ise check` includes every board's DRC errors. A board is done when `errors` is 0 and every net is routed; never call it ready otherwise.

Board objects, zones, placement, stackup and custom rules (`./ise pcb …` wraps each; ids or, with `--board <id>`, references like R1):

- **Graphics on any layer**: `pcb.graphic.create { board, layer, kind, …, width?, filled?, net?, locked? }`, layers: copper (`top`, `in1`…, `bottom`: real copper, joins `net`, pours keep clear, a copper graphic touching other copper is a short), `silk_top|silk_bottom`, `fab_top|fab_bottom`, `mask_top|mask_bottom` (openings), `paste_top|paste_bottom`, `courtyard_top|courtyard_bottom`, `user`, `comments` (KiCad names like `F.SilkS` work). Kinds: `line { points }`, `arc { center, radius, start, end }` or `{ through: [start, mid, end] }`, `circle { center, radius }`, `rect { from, to, corner? }`, `polygon { points }`, `bezier { points: 4 }`, `ellipse { center, rx, ry, rotation?, start?, end? }`, `text { text, at, size: cap height, rotation?, font?: "stroke" (default, fab-safe) | "Inter" (bundled) | font hash, weight?, align?: left|center|right, knockout?: true (letters cut from a filled box `margin` larger), mirror? (default: mirrored on bottom layers) }`, `image { at, size: width mm, px: [w, h], pixels: grey base64, threshold?, negative? }` (traced to filled art), `dimension { style: aligned|orthogonal|radial|leader|center, points, offset?, vertical?, text?: "<value> typ", units?: mm|inch|mil, precision?, text_size? }` (returns the measured `value`). `pcb.graphic.update { target, layer?, width?, shape?: {kind,…}, text? }`, `pcb.graphics.edit { board, layer?, kind?, width?, text_size?, font?, to_layer? }` (global edit). CLI: `./ise pcb text <board> silk_top "REV A" 30,2 --size 1.2 [--font Inter --knockout]`, `./ise pcb draw <board> fab_top dimension '{"style":"aligned","points":[[0,0],[50,0]],"offset":-3}'`, `./ise pcb image <board> silk_top logo.png 40,5 --size 8`.
- **Keepouts and rule areas**: `pcb.area.create { board, name, outline, layers?, no_tracks?, no_vias?, no_pads?, no_pours?, no_footprints?, placement?: ["U1", "R*"] }` (no flag given: keeps out tracks, vias and pours); violations `keepout`; a placement area warns `placement_area` when its parts leave it; rules name areas in `insideArea('name')`. `pcb.area.update`. CLI `./ise pcb keepout <board> Antenna 30,0 40,0 40,10 30,10 [--no tracks,vias,pours,footprints] [--layers top]`.
- **Zones**: besides net/layer/priority/min_width/islands/thermals: `hatch: { width, gap, angle?, border? }` (null for solid), `cutouts: [[[x,y]…]]`, `min_island_area` (mm²: only smaller dead islands removed), `name`. `pcb.zone.priority { target, to: raise|lower|top|bottom }`, `pcb.zone.duplicate { target, layer?, net?, outline? }`.
- **Teardrops**: `pcb.teardrops.set { board, enabled?: true, vias?, pads?, smd?, length_ratio?: 0.5, max_length?: 1, width_ratio?: 1, max_width?: 2, curved?: true, max_track_ratio?: 0.9 }`; they are worked out with the board (`board.teardrops`), skipped where they would break clearance, and go to Gerber/IPC-2581/ODB++/KiCad. CLI `./ise pcb teardrops <board> on|off`.
- **Vias**: `pcb.via.create { …, kind?: through|blind|buried|micro, from?, to?, stack?: { "in1": 0, "top": 0.8 } }` (blind: an outer layer to an inner one; buried: inner to inner; micro: neighbouring layers across one prepreg, defaults 0.1/0.25 mm; `stack` sets per-layer pads, 0 removes one). Checked: `via_span`, `microvia_crosses_core`, `microvia_drill` (rules `min_microvia_drill` 0.1, `min_microvia_diameter` 0.2), `microvia_aspect`, `microvia_stack`, `via_stack`. Blind/buried pairs get their own drill file (`<stem>-1-3.drl`). `pcb.via.update { targets, at?, drill?, diameter?, net?, kind?, from?, to?, stack? }`. Many at once: `pcb.via.stitch { board, zone? | outline?, net?, pitch?: 2.5, stagger?, drill?, diameter?, exclude?: [[x,y]] }` (a grid clear of other copper, holes, the edge and keepouts; stitching again replaces the group), `pcb.via.fence { board, net, track | points, pitch?: 1.5, offset?, sides?: both|left|right }`. CLI `./ise pcb stitch <board> GND --zone <id> --pitch 3`, `./ise pcb fence <board> <track> GND`.
- **Placement**: `pcb.move { targets, by? | to? | relative_to + offset?, rotate?, about? }` (move exactly, position relative), `pcb.align { targets, to: left|right|top|bottom|center_x|center_y, reference? }`, `pcb.distribute { targets, axis: x|y, by?: centers|gaps }`, `pcb.swap { a, b }`, `pcb.flip { targets, about_x? }` (to the other side, mirrored; copper and graphics to the mirror layer), `pcb.array { targets, grid: { nx, ny, dx, dy } | circular: { center, count, angle?, rotate? }, keep_nets? }` (components get the next free references, no nets unless `keep_nets`). Targets are components, tracks, vias, graphics, zones or rule areas; components move through `pcb.component.update` so their tracks follow. CLI `./ise pcb align left R1 R2 R3 --board <id>`, `./ise pcb array LED1 --board <id> --circular 50,50,12`.
- **Multichannel**: lay out and route one channel, then `pcb.channel.repeat { board, source: ["U1","R1","C1"], channels: [["U2","R2","C2"], {"U1":"U3","R1":"R9"}], step?: [dx, dy], routing?: true, areas?: false }`: matching parts (by footprint, then value, in reference order, or an explicit map) are placed like the source relative to each channel's anchor (or at source + k·step), tracks and vias inside the source channel are copied with nets mapped through matching pads (the target's old copper on those nets is replaced), `areas` adds a placement rule area per channel. CLI `./ise pcb channel <board> --source U1,R1 --to U2,R2 --to U3,R3 --areas`.
- **Stackup**: `pcb.stackup.set { board, layers?: 2…32, thickness?, dielectrics?: [{ kind: core|prepreg, thickness, material, epsilon_r?, loss_tangent? }] (layers − 1, top down), copper_oz?: [per layer], standard?, fit_thickness? }`; `board.stackup` (rows, total, custom) is in the board, a total off the finished thickness is a `stackup_thickness` warning, and it goes into the Gerber job, IPC-2581 and the KiCad export. Impedance targets on net classes are worked out from it (below). CLI `./ise pcb stackup <board> --layers 6`, `./ise pcb setup <board>`.
- **Routing constraints** (impedance, differential pairs, lengths, skew). Net classes carry electrical targets: `pcb.netclass.set { board, name, patterns?: ["USB_D*"], nets?, add_nets?, track_width?, clearance?, via_drill?, via_diameter?, neck_width?, impedance?: 50 (Ω single-ended), diff_impedance?: 90 (Ω, the class's pairs), diff_gap?: 0.15 (fixed gap: the width is solved for it; absent: gap ≈ width), impedance_tolerance?: 10 (%), max_uncoupled?, max_skew?, pair_via_pitch?, rename?, delete? }` (0 clears a target) answers with `layers`: per copper layer the width (and gap) that meets the target, Z0, Zdiff and delay (ps/mm), outer layers as microstrip over the next layer (Hammerstad–Jensen with thickness), inner as stripline between their neighbours (Cohn's offset stripline, Wheeler thickness), pairs edge-coupled (Cohn's exact odd mode inside, IPC-2141's term outside); neighbouring copper is taken as the reference planes, solder mask is not counted. Those widths are what the router, the pair router and the autorouter use on each layer, and DRC checks every controlled track (`impedance`, the tolerance; a neck under 1.5 mm into a pad is allowed narrower). Schematic classes take the same targets (`pcb.schematic.netclass { …, impedance?, diff_impedance?, diff_gap?, impedance_tolerance?, max_uncoupled?, max_skew? }`) and "Update board" carries them (and the patterns) to the board. Pairs are found from net names (`D+`/`D-`, `_P`/`_N`, `DP`/`DM`, `P`/`N`) or set: `pcb.pair.set { board, name, p, n, max_skew?, max_uncoupled?, delete? }`; `pcb.signal.set { board, detect_pairs?: false, pad_to_die?: { "U1.5": 1.2 } }`. Length groups: `pcb.length.group { board, name, nets: ["D0", "D?", "<pair name>"], target?, tolerance?, min?, max?, max_skew?, delete? }` (with a target each member is target ± tolerance (default 1 %); without, each is within tolerance of the longest). A net's length is its copper: tracks (arcs exact), each via's barrel between the outermost layers its tracks use (from the stackup) and pad-to-die; the board's `signal` has `lengths` (length, vias, via length, delay ps), `pairs` (lengths, skew, coupled and uncoupled length, gap per layer, Zdiff as routed), `groups` (members, target, spread) and `classes` (the per-layer targets). Checks: `impedance`, `diff_pair_gap` (each layer's gap ± 10 %), `diff_pair_uncoupled`, `skew` (pair, group spread), `length`, `via_count`. Routing a pair: `pcb.route.pair { board, pair, from?: ["J1.A6", "J1.A7"] (positive pad first), to?, steps?: [{ at, layer? }] (a new layer puts two coupled vias side by side, `pair_via_pitch` apart, the run going on straight out of them), layer?, mode?: walkaround|shove|highlight, width?, gap?, via_pitch?, corners?: "arc" }`: the centreline is laid as one line as wide as the pair (walkaround or shove), each track is it offset half a pitch (gap held exactly, arcs concentric), the pads are left square to their row and joined by short necks (narrower where they would crowd the partner's pad); it returns both lengths and the skew. `pcb.pair.drag { board, track, index, to, from?, mode? }` drags a segment with its partner's. `pcb.autoroute` routes each unrouted two-pad pair as a pair first (`pairs: false` to skip), then the rest. Tuning: `pcb.tune { board, net? | pair? | group? | track?, target?, mode?: "length" | "skew", style?: trombone|sawtooth, corner?: round|chamfer|square, amplitude?: 2 (pair 3), spacing?, radius?, side?: auto|left|right, tolerance?: 0.01, segment? }` meanders onto straight segments (longest first, fewest legs, each checked against everything around it) so the net lands on its target (a group's target or its longest member when not given); a pair is meandered as a pair (both tracks gain the same), then its skew taken out on the shorter track with small bumps away from the partner (`mode: "skew"` does only that); it returns before/after per net and notes when there is no room. The person has it in Nets › Net classes (targets, computed widths per layer), Differential pairs, Length matching (bars per member, Tune all), Net lengths; the board's Pair tool (D: click a pad of the pair, click corners, V for coupled vias, Enter) and Tune tool (T on a selected track: target, amplitude, spacing, style, corners, a live preview and readout), and the live length (and its target) while routing. Requirements: `intent.requirement.create { rule: { kind: "pcb_constraints", board, codes?: ["skew", …] | ["all"] } }` (no routing-constraint errors, or none of those codes) and `{ kind: "pcb_length", board, nets: ["D?"], target?, tolerance?, min?, max?, max_skew? }`; `./ise check` reports them. Exports: IPC-2581 `Spec`s with `Impedance` (value, tolerance, width, spacing, reference planes) referenced from their copper layers, ODB++ `matrix/stackup.xml` with impedances and `misc/impedance.txt`, the Gerber job's `ImpedanceControlled`, the fab package's `impedance.txt` and README note (stackup, controlled lines per layer, widths), `.kicad_pro` net classes (diff pair width/gap, patterns), `.kicad_dru` rules (track width per layer, diff_pair_gap, uncoupled, skew, length groups). CLI: `./ise pcb netclass <board> [<name> --impedance 50 | --diff 90 --gap 0.15 --tol 10 --patterns 'USB_D*' --max-skew 0.1 --max-uncoupled 3]`, `./ise pcb pair <board> [<name> <p> <n>]`, `./ise pcb group <board> <name> D0,D1,D2,D3 --tol 0.5 --max-skew 0.5`, `./ise pcb lengths <board>`, `./ise pcb tune <board> <net|pair|group> [--target mm] [--skew] [--amplitude 1] [--dry]`, `./ise pcb route-pair <board> <pair> [--step x,y[:layer]]… [--dry]`, `./ise pcb pad-to-die <board> U1.5=1.2`. Previews: `POST /pcb/<id>/router { op: "pair" | "pair_drag" | "tune", … }`. For a USB 2.0 pair: a class with `diff_impedance: 90`, a fixed gap the fab can hold, `max_skew` about 0.1 mm; route it with the pair router, tune the skew, then `./ise pcb lengths`.
- **Custom rules** (the KiCad `.kicad_dru` language, read by Iṣẹ́ Studio's own parser): `pcb.rules.set { board, text }` with `(version 1) (rule "name" (layer outer|inner|"F.Cu")? (condition "A.NetClass == 'HV' && B.NetClass != 'HV'")? (constraint clearance (min 1.5mm)) (severity error|warning|ignore)?)`. Properties `A.`/`B.`: Type (Track, Via, Pad, Zone, Footprint, Graphic, Text, Hole), NetName, NetClass, Layer, Reference, Footprint, Via_Type (Through, Blind/buried, Micro), Pad_Type, Width, Hole, Name; functions insideArea, enclosedByArea, intersectsArea, existsOnLayer, isPlated, hasNetclass; `*`/`?` wildcards; units mm, mil, in, um. Checked constraints: clearance, hole_clearance, hole_to_hole, edge_clearance, courtyard_clearance, track_width, via_diameter, hole_size, annular_width (min/max), disallow (track via micro_via buried_via pad zone text graphic hole footprint), and on whole nets: length (min/max; `opt` is the target), skew (max: across all nets a rule matches; a pair's own skew with `A.isCoupledDiffPair()`), diff_pair_gap (min/opt/max), diff_pair_uncoupled (max), via_count (max), and Iṣẹ́ Studio's `impedance` (Ω, min/max or opt ±10 %, per track: differential for a pair's tracks; KiCad does not read it, so the export keeps it as a comment); `A.inDiffPair('USB_D')`, `A.isCoupledDiffPair()` read the pairs; later rules win, board minima always hold. Violations name the rule; a file that does not read is `rules_syntax`. Exported as `<stem>.kicad_dru` (and in the KiCad bundle). CLI `./ise pcb rules <board> rules.kicad_dru`, `./ise pcb drc <board> [--code keepout]`.

KiCad's official libraries: `./ise pcb parts ldo 3.3` searches the symbols (`--footprints` the footprints) by name, description and keywords; `./ise pcb add <schematic> Regulator_Linear:AP2112K-3.3 --at 120,80` places one with its KiCad footprint defined on the board in the same step (`--footprint Package_SO:SOIC-8_3.9x4.9mm_P1.27mm` picks another; it warns about pins with no pad of that number, which then need `pin_map`). Under it are GET `/pcb/kicad/symbol/<Library:Name>` and `/pcb/kicad/footprint/<Library:Name>` and `pcb.schematic.place { …, symbol: "<Library:Name>", definition, footprint_definition }`; the instance carries the definition, and later placements of the same part need neither. `./ise pcb footprint <board> <Library:Name>` defines a footprint alone for `pcb.component.create`. The libraries download once (about 25 MB) to a cache on the person's computer; they are CC-BY-SA with KiCad's design exception (boards made with them are the person's own). The person searches them from the schematic's part library too. MPN and LCSC come along when the part number is known; say so when they do not.

Libraries, editors and builds (the person has all of it in the Electronics workspace's Library view: symbol and footprint editors, Logo, Assign footprints, Variants, Design blocks, Libraries):

- **Project libraries** live in the project (versioned, shared with the team): `pcb.lib.symbol.save { library?: "Project", symbol: <SymbolDef>, extends?: "Lib:Parent", power?: { net, style? }, rename_from? }` and `pcb.lib.footprint.save { library?, footprint, model?: { file?, offset: [x, y, z], rotation } }` add or replace a part (`Library:Name`); `pcb.lib.copy { kind: symbol|footprint, from: "R" | "Lib:Name", library?, name? }` duplicates a built-in or project part to edit; `pcb.lib.delete { symbols?, footprints? }`; `pcb.lib.import { library, symbols, footprints }` brings many at once. `./ise pcb lib` lists them, `./ise pcb lib symbol|footprint <id>` shows one with its checker findings, `./ise pcb lib check` checks them all (errors also show in `./ise check`), `./ise pcb lib copy <name | Library:Name> [--footprint] [--to Lib]` copies built-in, project or KiCad parts (a KiCad symbol brings its footprint), `./ise pcb lib svg <id> [--footprint]` exports a drawing. A SymbolDef is `{ name, prefix, value, description, footprint, footprints?, mpn?, lcsc?, keywords?, fields?: { Datasheet: … }, pins: [{ number, name, at: [x, y] (sheet mm, y down, the connection end, on the 1.27 grid), side: left|right|up|down (the way it leaves the body), length, etype, shape?: inverted|clock|inverted_clock|input_low|clock_low|output_low|edge_clock_high|non_logic, unit? (0 = every unit), hidden?, pads? }], units: [[gfx…] per unit] (gfx: { kind: rect, a, b, fill: none|body|outline } | line { pts, width } | poly { pts, fill } | circle { c, r, fill } | arc { c, r, start, end } | text { at, text, size }), demorgan?: [[gfx…] per unit], demorgan_pins?: { "<pin>": shape }, show_pin_numbers, show_pin_names }`. Derived symbols (`extends`) take the parent's pins and body and keep their own name, value, footprint and fields; power symbols place as power ports of their net. Place with `pcb.lib.place { schematic, symbol: "Lib:Name", at, unit?, body_style?: 2, reference?, footprint? }` (`./ise pcb lib place`; its library footprint goes on the board); `pcb.lib.body_style { targets, style: 1|2 }` switches placed parts to the De Morgan body; `pcb.lib.symbol.push { symbol }` / `pcb.lib.footprint.push { footprint }` bring library edits to placed parts and boards (placed symbols carry a copy, like KiCad's).
- **Checkers**: the symbol checker flags duplicate pin numbers, pins off the 50 mil grid, stacked pins that are not one signal, hidden power inputs (Iṣẹ́ Studio joins nothing to hidden pins), pins pointing into the body, units without pins, numbering gaps, and pins whose pads the footprint lacks (and pads no pin reaches); the footprint checker flags pads that short or sit closer than the clearance, rings and drills under the rules, holes outside their copper, courtyards that miss copper, silk on pads, broken custom outlines, paste outside its pad, missing pad 1. Fix errors before saving a part as done.
- **Pads** take, besides rect/round_rect/circle/oval/custom: `chamfer: { ratio, corners: [top_left…] }` and `trapezoid: [dx, dy]` (written as an exact outline), `stack: { inner?: { shape, size }, opposite?: {…}, remove_inner? }` (through-hole copper per layer), `zone_connection: thermal|solid|none`, `thermal_gap`, `thermal_spoke` (this pad's relief, over the zone's), `drill_offset: [x, y]` (hole from the copper centre), `no_paste`. KiCad imports keep chamfers, trapezoids and offset drills exactly.
- **Wizards** (IPC-7351B, density A/B/C): `./ise pcb lib wizards` lists presets (chips 0201–2512, SOIC/MSOP/TSSOP/SSOP, LQFP, QFN/DFN with exposed pads, paste windows and thermal vias, SOT-23/-5/-6/223/89, BGA with JEDEC row letters and depopulation, DIP, headers and connectors with pegs); `./ise pcb lib wizard <preset> [key=value…] [--save Library] [--board <id>]` runs one with changes (`pins=14 pitch=0.65 'span=[6.2,6.6]'`, ranges as [min, max] from the datasheet); POST `/pcb/libs/wizard` takes the same JSON. Prefer a wizard over hand-placed pads for standard packages, and cite the datasheet's dimensions you used.
- **Footprint assignment**: `./ise pcb assign <schematic>` lists every part with the footprints that fit its pads; `./ise pcb assign <schematic> R1=R_0402 U3=MyParts:QFN-24_4x4` assigns (`pcb.lib.assign { schematic, footprints }`, project-library footprints go on the board, pins without a pad are reported).
- **Logos** (bitmap to component): `./ise pcb logo <image.png|.pgm> --size <mm> [--layer silk|copper|symbol] [--threshold 128] [--negative] [--name N] [--save Library] [--board <id> --at x,y]` traces the image into a silkscreen logo (filled with silk strokes), an exposed-copper logo (no net, no paste) or a schematic graphic, saves it, and can place it (POST `/pcb/libs/bitmap`).
- **Global libraries** sit on the person's computer (shared by every project, never synced): `./ise pcb lib global list | export <name> [--library L] | import <name> [--to L] | delete <name>`. `pcb.lib.table.set { libraries: [{ name, kind: project|global|kicad|builtin, enabled, pinned }] }` (or `./ise pcb lib table Name:kind[:pinned][:off] …`) is the project's library table: switched-off libraries are not offered, pinned ones first.
- **Assembly variants** (`pcb.variant.create { schematic, name, dnp?, fitted?, overrides?, copy_from? }`, `pcb.variant.update { target, parts: { R7: { dnp: true }, U2: { value, mpn, lcsc } } }`, `pcb.variant.delete`): one board, built several ways; a new value drops the design's part numbers unless the variant gives them. `./ise pcb variant <schematic> list | add <name> [--dnp R1,R2] [--fit R5] [--copy Other] | set <name> R3.value=4k7 R3.lcsc=C23162 R7.dnp=true | bom <name> [--format jlcpcb] | delete <name>`; GET `/pcb/<board>/variant/<name>/bom.csv|positions.csv|fab.zip`.
- **Design blocks**: `./ise pcb block save <schematic> <name> R5 D2 … | --sheet <s> [--description …] [--replace]` keeps symbols, the wires, labels and notes among them, and (when on a board) their layout and copper; `./ise pcb block place <schematic> <name> --at x,y [--board-at x,y]` places it with fresh references, its local labels kept apart from ones already on the sheet (global labels and power ports keep their names: connect the block's interface yourself), its parts laid out on the board as saved with tracks and vias on the new nets; `./ise pcb block list | delete <name>` (`pcb.block.save|place|update|delete`).

Trust before ordering: `./ise pcb verify-footprints` compares every built-in footprint with KiCad's pad by pad (kind, position, size, shape, drill); errors mean a part may not fit, warnings are land-size choices, notes are reviewed differences where Iṣẹ́ Studio follows the maker's drawing. `./ise pcb gerber-check <board>` reads the fab files back with a reader separate from the writer, paints them at 0.02 mm and compares with the board: copper area per layer and per net, every pad exposed, pins, shorts between nets, mask openings, paste, every hole, the outline. Run both before saying a board is ready to order; the Fab tab shows the layers as read back and the same check.

Simulation (ngspice, run in batch): `./ise simulate <schematic>` turns the schematic into a SPICE netlist and runs a transient (`--tran 30ms`), DC sweep (`--dc VBUS:0:6:0.05`), AC (`--ac VBUS:10:1e6`) or `--op`. Parts get models from their symbol and value: R/C (ESR; `--derate 0.6` for MLCC DC bias)/L/fuse exact; diodes, LEDs, transistors generic; push buttons (`--press SW2@20ms:5ms`); a USB-C receptacle is a 5 V source through 0.2 Ω (`--source NET=5V,r=0.2,rise=1ms` adds or replaces a supply); LDOs (ME6211, AMS1117, XC6206, AP2112, or any "3.3V" LDO) behavioural from their datasheets; the ESP32 module is a load that runs when EN > 0.75·VDD with a Wi-Fi burst (`--burst U1@5ms:2ms:0.5A`). Everything left out is listed; models marked approximate are approximate: say so with the numbers. Each model brings its datasheet checks (the ESP32's 3.0–3.6 V supply and tSTBL ≥ 50 µs, a regulator's current rating and dissipation); add expectations with `--expect` (repeatable): functions `min max avg pp` over a window (`burst`, `running`, `all`, or two times), `final`, `at(V(x), 5ms)`, `cross(V(EN), 2.475)`, `fall(…)`, `settle(V(3V3), 2%)`, `rise(V(3V3))`, signals `V(net)`, `V(a,b)`, `I(part)`, units allowed, e.g. `--expect "min(V(3V3), burst) > 3.0" --expect "cross(V(EN), 2.475) - rise(V(3V3)) > 50us"`. `--save "Wi-Fi burst"` keeps it (`pcb.simulation.save { schematic, name, request }`): `./ise check` then runs it and fails on a failing check or expectation. The person has the same in the Simulate tab, with plots.

Other tools: `pcb.board.import_kicad { text, name?, at? }` makes a board from a `.kicad_pcb` file's text (KiCad 6–9: outline, 2 or 4 layers, footprints with every pad shape including custom, tracks and arcs, vias, zones with their settings, nets, references, values; 3D models ignored; body heights estimated) and returns `notes` on anything approximated; the person drops the file on the view or uses Import in the Electronics workspace. GET `/pcb/<id>/file/<stem>.kicad_pcb` (KiCad 8), `<stem>.emn` / `<stem>.emp` (IDF 3.0 for MCAD) and `<stem>.step` (the 3D board, exact). They are checked by round trips and parsers here; say a cross-check in KiCad itself is still worth doing.

Interchange with every other EDA tool (DE-E3). `pcb.import { file, text | data (base64, for binary), format?, name?, at?, board?, files? }` reads, telling the format from the content: KiCad `.kicad_pcb`, `.kicad_sch` (sub-sheets given in `files` by name) and project bundles (a zip of `.kicad_pro`/`.kicad_pcb`/`.kicad_sch`: board, schematic linked to it, net classes), Eagle `.brd`/`.sch` (XML), EasyEDA Standard JSON (PCB and schematic) and Pro (`.epro` zip or `.epcb`; Pro schematics not yet), Altium `.PcbDoc`/`.SchDoc` (binary OLE or ASCII; one schematic sheet), CADSTAR `.cpa`, Allegro Fabmaster extracts, PADS ASCII (mils/metric/inches), gEDA/pcb. Boards come in through the same path as KiCad (footprints rebuilt from each part's pads, identical ones shared; outline from the edge layer, else a box round everything; more than four copper layers keep the outer two and first two inner), schematics with each symbol carrying the drawing and pins the file had, nets as wires, labels and power ports. The result lists `notes` on anything approximated: read them to the person. `./ise pcb import <file>` does it from the command line; the person uses Import in the Electronics workspace (or drops `.kicad_pcb`, `.kicad_sch`, `.brd`, `.sch`, `.PcbDoc`, `.SchDoc`, `.epro`, `.cpa`, `.asc`, `.pcb` on the view). Importers are written from the formats' published structure and tested on fixtures written here, not on files from those tools: on a real file, check the board's DRC and nets after importing and say so.
Writing: `GET /pcb/<id>/exports` lists everything (and what imports), `GET /pcb/<id>/file/<stem><suffix>`: `.kicad_pro` (net classes and rules), `-kicad.zip` (project bundle), `.kicad_sch` (the board's schematic; Iṣẹ́ Studio symbols travel as `ise:<name>` and come back as themselves, power ports as `power:<net>`), netlists `.net` (KiCad S-expression), `-netlist.xml`, `-orcad.net`, `-pads.net`, `-allegro.net`, `-cadstar.frp` (from the schematic when there is one, else the board), `.d356` (IPC-D-356A bare-board test), `-ipc2581.xml` (IPC-2581 rev C), `-odb.zip` (ODB++ v8 tree), `-job.gbrjob` (Gerber job file), `-drill-map.gbr|svg|pdf`, `-drill-report.txt`, `-board.svg` (all layers in colour), `-<layer>.svg` (one layer, e.g. `-F_Cu.svg`), `-board.pdf` (a page per layer), `.wrl` (VRML 2.0), `.glb` (glTF binary), `-both.pos` and `-pos.csv` (KiCad position files: footprint origins), `-top-pnp.gbr`/`-bottom-pnp.gbr` (Gerber X3 component layers). A schematic alone: `GET /pcb/schematic/<id>/file/<stem>.kicad_sch`, `-kicad-sch.zip` (every sheet), the netlists, `-sheet<n>.svg`. Plots are drawn from the Gerbers as read back, so they show what the fab gets. The Fab tab lists these under "For other EDA tools".

Outputs (DE-853): Gerber RS-274X with X2 attributes per layer (copper with net/pin attributes, mask, paste, silk with designators, Edge_Cuts) and Excellon PTH/NPTH, Protel names: GET `/pcb/<id>/file/<name>` (names in `files`), `/pcb/<id>/file/bom.csv?format=jlcpcb|pcbway|generic`, `/pcb/<id>/file/positions.csv?format=…` (JLCPCB CPL: Designator, Mid X, Mid Y, Layer, Rotation; coordinates from the board's lower-left corner), and `/pcb/<id>/fab.zip?fab=jlcpcb|pcbway|oshpark|eurocircuits|aisler` for the whole package with a readme. Placement rotations follow IPC-7351 zero orientation: tell the person to check them in the fab's assembly preview.

Etching a board at home with a fiber laser (EZCAD, LightBurn): GET `/pcb/<id>/file/<stem>-laser-<layer>.dxf|.svg|.bmp|-README.txt` or `<stem>-laser.zip`, with query `layer`, `isolate` (mm ring burned around the copper; 0, the default, burns off all copper that is not the circuit), `pilot` (drill-start dot, default 0.5 mm), `mirror` (default: mirrored for the bottom layer) and `dpi` (bitmap, default 1000). The art is centred on (0, 0) for the laser's field; DXF layer ETCH is closed outlines to hatch, EDGE the board outline; the bitmap is 1-bit, black burns. The README gives EZCAD steps and starting MOPA settings: say they are starting points and suggest a test board (trace-width and gap ladders) first. Design such boards single-sided with wide traces and gaps (0.3 mm or more) unless the person's test board shows finer works.

Where to get it: `fabs` in `/pcb/<id>` checks the board as designed against each fab's published limits (track, gap, holes, rings, edge, thickness, finish, mask colour, size) with what fails and why; an `estimate` appears only for fabs that publish their formula (OSH Park, Aisler). No fab documents prefilled quote links: give the quote page and the specs to enter. `bom` lists components merged by MPN, with LCSC numbers and JLCPCB Basic/Extended where known, and distributor search links (LCSC, Digi-Key, Mouser, Farnell, Arrow, TME, Octopart); record a choice with `pcb.sourcing.set { board, key: "<MPN>", supplier, sku, unit_price, currency }`. Nothing is fetched or sent: no distributor has a keyless API, so live prices are not available (keys can be stored on the person's computer for later). In the project BOM (`/bom/project`) each board is a `pcb_fab` Make line and its components are Buy lines; GET `/pcb/buy` gives every board's Buy lines merged by MPN. The person has all of this in the Electronics workspace (L): the schematic (Schematic / Both / Board: symbols, wires, labels, ERC markers, a searchable part library, W wire, N label, U power port, Q no-connect, R turn, X mirror; selecting a part or net selects it on the board too; Sync shows the change report and updates the board), the board in 2D with layers, ratsnest and DRC markers (drag parts and their tracks come along; draw tracks, V drops a via and changes layer), and beside either or both the side panel: parts and nets (the eye hides one on the board, view only), checks, fab (with the read-back preview and check), BOM, and Simulate. `examples/pcb-esp32` is a worked 25-part board (USB-C power, LDO, ESP32 module, buttons, LEDs, headers) that routes, passes DRC and exports its package.

Fab utilities (none of them changes the project):
- Calculators: `./ise pcb calc` lists them, `./ise pcb calc <id> key=value…` answers (GET `/pcb/calc/<id>?…`), each with its source and caveats: `track` (width for a current and rise by IPC-2221 or the IPC-2152 baseline fit, or `width=` for the current it carries; resistance, drop, loss over `length`), `via` (barrel resistance, thermal resistance, current for a rise, capacitance, inductance), `pth` (hole and land for a lead by producibility level and class), `spacing` (IPC-2221B table 6-1 for a voltage, every column), `classes` (IPC-6012 classes, IPC-2221 levels), `impedance` (`line=microstrip|stripline|cpw|gcpw`, `width height thickness er gap`, `pair=` gap for differential; closed forms, not a field solver: say so and point to the fab's stackup for controlled impedance), `attenuator` (pi, tee, bridged-tee, splitter), `eseries`, `resistors` (closest 1, 2 or 3 standard parts to a target), `colour` (bands for `value`, or `bands=yellow,violet,red,gold` for the value), `regulator` (`kind=feedback|3-terminal`; solve R1 or Vout, nearest standard pair), `wavelength`, `wire` (AWG), `fusing` (Onderdonk), `galvanic` (anodic index of two metals). Use them instead of arithmetic in your head when choosing a track width, a via count for a current, a mains spacing or a divider.
- Panels: `./ise pcb panel <board> rows=2 cols=3 [separation=mousebites|vscore|tabs] [frame=rails-tb|rails-lr|frame|none] [gap=2 tab_width=3 tabs=1 bite_drill=0.5 bite_spacing=0.8 bite_offset=0.25 rail=5 fiducials=true fiducial_copper=1 fiducial_opening=2 tooling=true tooling_hole=1.5] [--fab jlcpcb] [--out panel.zip]` lays out a grid panel (KiKit-style: substrate = boards ∪ tabs ∪ rails, profile = its outline; mouse bites on each tab where it meets a board; V-cuts edge to edge on a `Vcut` layer; three fiducials and four tooling holes on the rails), reports problems (tabs that miss a non-rectangular outline, V-scoring a shape that is not a rectangle, rails too narrow, a gap under the router bit, a panel in pieces) and reads every panel file back with the independent reader. The zip (GET `/pcb/<id>/panel.zip?…`) holds the panel Gerbers and drills (each copy's copper with its X2 net attributes) and positions/BOM for every copy, designators suffixed `_<board>` (board 1 bottom left, along the rows). Tabs sit on the board's bounding box, so they suit rectangular boards; say so for other shapes.
- Gerber viewer: `./ise pcb gerbview <files or zips…>` (or `--board <id>` for a board's own package) reads any Gerber/Excellon set: each layer's function (X2, else guessed from the name — say when guessed), objects, apertures, nets, tools; `--compare <older zip or files>` reports per layer the area added and removed (holes added/removed for drills); `--pdf out.pdf` draws the layers; `--to-board steps.json [--name …]` writes steps that rebuild a board from the files (outline and cutouts, tracks with their X2 nets, vias) for `./ise run` — pads and pours do not become footprints or zones, so say the parts must be placed again. POST `/pcb/gerbview { files: [{ name, data: base64 }], against?, summary? }`, `/pcb/gerbview/pdf`. The person has it as Gerbers in the Electronics header: layer list with colour, visibility and order, flip, dim others, highlight by net, part or D-code, click to inspect an object's attributes, measure, D-code list, show the source, compare two revisions, export PNG/SVG/PDF.
- 3D: `./ise pcb glb <board> [--out board.glb]` (GET `/pcb/<id>/board.glb`) writes the populated board as binary glTF (laminate in the mask colour with holes, pads in the finish, silkscreen, bodies). In the 3D view the person can show or hide the mask, silkscreen, copper and bodies, parts by type (SMD, through-hole, other, DNP), bounding boxes, and save a PNG or glTF of the board.
